verdict.headline: scripts/validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs still puts the socket credential in the query string. server.js has REFUSED a URL-borne credential since PR #1357 (2026-08-25). The server is behaving exactly as designed; the validator is the stale caller.
verdict.rejectingCondition: server.js:855-863 -- `if (firstQueryValue(parsedUrl.query.token)) { console.warn(... reason=token-in-url); rejectUpgrade(socket, '400 Bad Request'); return; }`
verdict.validatorFault: scripts/validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs:257 appends `&token=<wireToken>` to the wsUrl, and :260 constructs `new WebSocket(url, { perMessageDeflate: false })` with NO subprotocol list -- so the credential arrives only in the URL, which is the one place the server now rejects outright.
verdict.loopbackHostnameRuledOut: The listener bound 127.0.0.1/IPv4 and emitted a valid MEKSTATION_LISTENER_READY record; the POST /api/multiplayer/matches on the same origin returned 201. Host-header / loopback-bind is NOT implicated -- an identical WS handshake to the same host:port succeeded in arm B of the reproduction.

secondDefect_uncaughtRejection.summary: openAndJoin() registers TWO ws.once('error') handlers against the same socket, each of which schedules a 500 ms setTimeout that rejects a DIFFERENT promise. Only one of those promises has a consumer at the moment the error fires, so the other rejects with no handler attached and Node's default unhandled-rejections=throw mode kills the process.
mechanism: validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs:278 -- `replayPromise` is CONSTRUCTED but not awaited yet (the await is at :396).

validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs:333-348 -- inside replayPromise, `ws.once('error', ...)` schedules setTimeout(..., 500) whose callback builds the 'Socket errored before ReplayEnd' Error at :337-:344 and rejects replayPromise.
validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs:351-375 -- the open-promise is constructed SECOND and IS awaited immediately; its own ws.once('error') at :361 schedules a second setTimeout(..., 500).
The 400 makes `ws` emit a single 'error'. Both once-handlers fire. Both timers are armed in the same tick with the same 500 ms delay, and the replayPromise timer was armed FIRST, so it fires FIRST.
replayPromise therefore rejects while nothing is attached to it -> unhandledRejection -> Node throws it as a top-level uncaught exception.

The recorded stack `at Timeout._onTimeout (validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs:337:13)` points at exactly that Error construction site, confirming the unhandled one is the replayPromise rejection, not the awaited open-promise rejection.
consequences: The process dies on the uncaught exception instead of unwinding, so `openAndJoin`'s `finally { ws.close() }` (:397-399) and `runCamp00Authority`'s `finally { fs.rmSync(nextDist, ...) }` (:500) never run.

This is why the receipt run observed .next surviving the failure -- the nextDirCleanupAnomaly in camp00-receipt-run-20260915.json is a SYMPTOM of this defect, and its 'UNVERIFIED / INFERENCE' explanation is now confirmed correct.
It also destroys the diagnostic: the useful, context-rich message (which promise, which frames, which server output) is replaced by a bare uncaught throw, and main()'s catch at :579-582 never prints.
secondDefect_uncaughtRejection.smallestCorrectFix: Attach an inert catch to replayPromise the moment it is created, so a rejection that arrives before :396 is never unhandled: `replayPromise.catch(() => {})` immediately after :349. The awaited rejection at :396 still surfaces normally (a promise may carry any number of handlers). Optionally also hoist a single shared `ws.once('error')` instead of two, but the one-line guard is sufficient and minimal.

proposedFix.classification: VALIDATOR-DEFECT -- the fix is entirely inside the validator; server.js is correct and MUST NOT be relaxed
proposedFix.explicitNonFix: Do NOT re-permit the URL credential in server.js. #1357 removed it deliberately (a bearer token in a query string lands in access logs, proxy logs and crash reports), the refusal is what keeps the header carrier a guarantee rather than an option, and serverCredentialMirror.test.ts + socketCredentialProtocol.test.ts + client.test.ts pin that behaviour.

changes.change: Add the subprotocol constants and the base64url transform, mirroring src/lib/multiplayer/socketCredentialProtocol.ts: WS_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 'mekstation.v1', WS_CREDENTIAL_PREFIX = 'mekstation.token.', toBase64Url(b64) = b64.replace(/\+/g,'-').replace(/\//g,'_').replace(/=+$/,''), credentialProtocols(wire) = [WS_PROTOCOL_VERSION, WS_CREDENTIAL_PREFIX + toBase64Url(wire)].
changes.why: The script is ESM .mjs run by bare node with no TS loader, so it cannot import the .ts module. This is the same constraint that forced the server.js mirror, and it gets the same treatment: a mirror plus a test that refuses to let the copies drift.
removes the URL credential that trips server.js:855

changes.change: `const ws = new WebSocket(url, { perMessageDeflate: false });`  ->  `const ws = new WebSocket(url, credentialProtocols(wireToken), { perMessageDeflate: false });`
changes.why: supplies the credential through Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, matching client.ts:690-693
the independent robustness defect above -- keeps a pre-await rejection from becoming an unhandled rejection that kills the process and skips both finally blocks

This defect existed for 21 days precisely because nothing read this file.
regressionTest.tierNote: The live proof that the whole journey works remains the camp-00 receipt run itself; the mirror test exists so the next carrier change cannot silently break it again.
regressionTest.provenFixture: Arm B of the reproduction in this document is the passing fixture: credentialProtocols(scopelessWireToken) against the packaged standalone server yields ReplayStart/ReplayChunk/ReplayEnd.
